## 1. This week's analysis

```{bash}

mkdir -p ../output/03.2-eDNA # create a file directory 
cd ../output/03.2-eDNA # set working directory

raw=$(realpath ../../data/raw/eDNA-yellow_island-2023) # Assign pathway to a varbale name

# manifest: sample name, R1 path, R2 path
printf "sample-id\tforward-absolute-filepath\treverse-absolute-filepath\n" > manifest.tsv

for sample in Site1a_S83 Site1b_S84 Site1c_S85 Site5a_S87 Site5b_S88 Site5c_S89; do #list of samples
  printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n" \
    "$sample" \
    "${raw}/Yell_July18_${sample}_R1_001.fastq.gz" \
    "${raw}/Yell_July18_${sample}_R2_001.fastq.gz" >> manifest.tsv
done

# metadata: sample name, site
printf "sample-id\tsite\n"          > sample-metadata.tsv
printf "Site1a_S83\tSite1\n"       >> sample-metadata.tsv
printf "Site1b_S84\tSite1\n"       >> sample-metadata.tsv
printf "Site1c_S85\tSite1\n"       >> sample-metadata.tsv
printf "Site5a_S87\tSite5\n"       >> sample-metadata.tsv
printf "Site5b_S88\tSite5\n"       >> sample-metadata.tsv
printf "Site5c_S89\tSite5\n"       >> sample-metadata.tsv

cat manifest.tsv
cat sample-metadata.tsv

```

## 2. Reflection questions

1. What is the difference between mapping reads to a reference and assembling reads without one?

> Mapping is when there is already a genome for a species and you are just comparing your read to the exhisting read. In assembly reads are assembled into longer strings when there is no existing genome to try and reconstruct the sequences.  

2. What intermediate summary would you inspect before trusting a mapping or quantification result?

> I would look at check sums and run the head function to make sure the first few rows of the data look right.  

3.What is the smallest meaningful workflow slice you can run for your project this week?

> I can run 6 sites through the trimming process and then start working on the manifest to make sure all of the code is running correctly. Once it is running then I can add in the rest of the sites as well as start running QIIM.
